findings.title: Sidecar .sha256 files are not produced by `php artisan foodking:backup-daily`
findings.evidence: ls storage/backups/db-daily/*.sha256 → zsh: no matches found. RunDailyBackup.php writes only the .sql.gz, no sidecar.
findings.impact: The official restore script scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh requires the sidecar (line 38: `[[ -f "$SHA" ]] || fail "checksum sidecar missing: $SHA"`). A first-responder reaching for that script against a storage/backups/ artifact will get an immediate hard fail and have to fall back to manual gunzip | mysql (what this drill did). The production cron path (scripts/backup-foodking-daily.sh writing to /var/backups/foodking/) DOES produce .sha256 — so the gap exists only for the Laravel-cmd lane.
findings.disposition: V1.0.2 backlog — either (a) extend RunDailyBackup to emit .sha256 alongside the .sql.gz, or (b) update scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh to accept --skip-checksum when sidecar absent, or (c) document the two-track separation in BACKUP_RESTORE_NF525.md runbook so on-call knows the storage/backups/ lane requires manual checksum verification.
findings.rationale_non_blocking: Today's V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne single-box deployment uses the Laravel cmd lane scheduled via Kernel.php — restore drill via direct gunzip | mysql verified working empirically here AND in the committed RESTORE_DRILL_2026-05-21.md doc. Production /var/backups/foodking/ cron lane separately produces sidecars and is what scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh targets.

findings.title: Backup size 166 KB < 1 MB warn floor on fresh local DB
findings.evidence: `dump under warn-bytes threshold (166347 < 1048576) — plausible on fresh local DB but verify` — warn line in backup-run.txt
findings.impact: Owner intent (RunDailyBackup.php docblock) is to surface suspiciously small dumps on a real restaurant DB. On dev (134 orders / 67 audit_logs / 59 items) 166 KB is plausible. In production with 1000+ daily orders this floor would surface real truncation. Not a defect.
findings.disposition: Informational — keep threshold as-is. The warn (not fail) discipline is correct.

findings.title: ≥7-day-old / monthly / quarterly backups do not yet exist — 6-year retention rotation path not empirically observable today
findings.evidence: Verified by `ls -lt storage/backups/db-monthly/` and `ls -lt storage/backups/db-quarterly/` both returning empty (only `.gitkeep` placeholder). storage/backups/db-daily/ has 2 artifacts: daily-2026-05-21 (2d) + daily-2026-05-23 (today). Oldest dump available = 2 days old. RunDailyBackup.php rotate() seeds monthly only on day-of-month==1 and quarterly only on Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct day-1 — V1 LOCAL deployment is still inside its first month, so structurally no monthly artifact exists yet.
findings.impact: Task G.12.4 asked for empirical verification of ≥7d-old backup restorability to prove the 6-year retention path. We can prove (a) daily-tier restorability bit-identically (done — see restore_drill_fresh_backup + restore_drill_older_backup sections), and (b) the rotation code path STRUCTURALLY (read of RunDailyBackup::rotate at lines 325-388). We CANNOT today prove empirically that the rotation actually emits monthly/quarterly artifacts and that those artifacts also round-trip — there are no such artifacts to test against.
findings.disposition: Re-run G.12 cycle: (1) on day-1 of the next calendar month to verify a monthly-YYYY-MM.sql.gz appears in db-monthly/, restore it, verify CHAIN OK. (2) on first Jul 1 / Oct 1 / Jan 1 to verify a quarterly-YYYY-Qn.sql.gz appears in db-quarterly/, restore it, verify CHAIN OK. (3) cron task scheduled to auto-run the drill quarterly (suggestion from RESTORE_DRILL_2026-05-21.md §'Future drill cadence'). Until then, the 24-quarter NF525 retention is structurally-implemented but empirically-unproven for tiers 2 and 3.
findings.rationale_non_blocking: V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne ship date is BEFORE first month-rollover would produce a monthly artifact. The daily tier — which is what the restaurant relies on for next-day restorability — is fully verified. Monthly/quarterly tiers serve longer-term NF525 audit (6-year inspector retrieval) and will be validatable once first rotation actually emits. No code change required — the rotation logic is in place and code-inspected GREEN; only the empirical attestation is deferred.

verdict_rationale: Fresh backup at HEAD (commit 69279bc85) produced successfully — gzip integrity OK, SHA256 recorded.
Full restore round-trip executed empirically into foodking_restore_test → all 88 tables + 67 audit_logs + 6 z_reports + 134 orders + 59 items restored bit-identical to source (counts match exactly).
audit_logs first hash + last hash + z_reports last signature bit-identical between source and restored — chain pointer integrity proven.
`php artisan fiscal:verify-chain --all` returns CHAIN OK on restored DB — restored chain re-verifies under the live algorithm.
Forensic HMAC walk on 5 audit_logs rows: 5/5 PASS — recomputed HMAC equals stored current_hash, confirming both payload preservation AND branch_secret accessibility post-restore.

Older backup (daily-2026-05-21.sql.gz, 2 days old) restored independently into foodking_restore_old → 62/0/38/59/88 matches committed RESTORE_DRILL_2026-05-21.md proof exactly. Chain OK. SHA256 of the committed dump still bit-identical to value recorded in the proof doc 2 days ago — proves no silent file tampering. CAVEAT: task asked for ≥7d-old backup; the 2d-old artifact is the OLDEST available because V1 deployment is still inside its first month and monthly/quarterly dirs are empty (see G12-F-03).
NF525 BEFORE DELETE + BEFORE UPDATE triggers on audit_logs + z_reports preserved across both restored DBs — immutability invariant survives backup round-trip (mysqldump --triggers flag honoured).

Env-override probe airtight: re-restored fresh backup into foodking_restore_verify, confirmed `DB::connection()->getDatabaseName()` echoes the test DB name (not source), confirmed verifyChain runs against restored chain. No config cache present (bootstrap/cache/config.php absent) so DB_DATABASE override is picked up at runtime.
Test DBs (foodking_restore_test + foodking_restore_old + foodking_restore_verify) cleaned up. Source DB untouched.

Three non-blocking findings: P2 sidecar gap (G12-F-01), P3 warn threshold on dev DB (G12-F-02), P2 monthly/quarterly rotation empirically-unobservable until first rotation cycle (G12-F-03). None breaks the V1 restore path.
